3aad83f411.q: How can manufacturers enforce correct sales process behavior through system design rather than just documentation?
3aad83f411.a: Rather than writing SOPs that nobody reads, systems should be designed such that you cannot break process. Andy uses industrial engineering principles: make the system work only if the correct process is followed. This is the poke-yoke approach—designing systems that force compliance, similar to how RFID scanners could prevent material access unless tags were scanned, ensuring behavior change through system constraint rather than voluntary adherence.
